messages:
olivia: quick question for the partners thread — we're modeling committed vs ephemeral GPU supply for the marketplace pricing doc. can partners confirm whether reserved instances are billed on a per-hour calendar basis or rounded to the nearest minute? thinking about how to project $/token under mixed load.

samir: short answer: vendor A bills hourly with pro-rata for partial hours; vendor B bills by minute. that's why you see step changes in our cost curve. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

marco: also watch out for early-termination fees on 12+ month commits — they're charged as a % of remaining committed value, not pro-rated usage. that shows up as a separate invoice line, not in the usage records.

olivia: ugh ok. can we get the exact invoice line names so finance can map? we need the CSV column names to match in the cost model.

elaine: vendor-bot posted the mapping last quarter but i can paste the small table: Reserved -> "commitment_charge", Early termination -> "commit_early_fee", Spot -> "ephemeral_usage", Marketplace listing fee -> "map_listing_fee". not exhaustive but covers the common lines.

samir: one more nuance: spot preemption credits on some clouds are applied as a negative line called "spot_credit" vs a per-instance discount. we should model that as a separate rebate rather than lowering gross unit price.

marco: re: billing granularity for reserved: if you expect short-lived bursts, minute-billing partners look cheaper on paper but hourly billing + burst-capacity pool may actually be better once you add burst premium (typically +10-20%). we need a sim that folds in burst uplift.

olivia: yes — can someone sketch the sim inputs? thinking: (base_reserved_rate, billing_granularity, early_term_pct, burst_uplift_pct, spot_availability_prob). maybe a simple example JSON we can run in the cost model.

samir: example we use in modeling:```
{
  base_reserved_rate: 3.00, // $/GPU-hour
  billing_granularity: "hour", // or "minute"
  early_term_pct: 0.15, // percent of remaining commit if terminated
  burst_uplift_pct: 0.12,
  spot_availability_prob: 0.6
}
```

elaine: vendor-bot: can you confirm whether partner 'AtlasCompute' exposes an API to query available reserved capacity windows (i.e., how many reserved GPUs they have free for a 30/90/365 day window)? @vendor-bot

vendor-bot: AtlasCompute API: GET /v1/capacity/reserved?window_days={30|90|365} returns availability and price tiers. rate limits apply. docs: https://partners.atlascompute.io/api#capacity (internal link)

olivia: perfect. last thing — do partners provide region-level spot volatility metrics (historical preemption rates)? we need that to convert spot_availability_prob into scenario buckets.

samir: some do. ask for a CSV of daily preemption rates over 90 days. if they only give aggregate stats, we run Monte Carlo with a beta distribution to emulate volatility.

marco: action items: @elaine pull invoice line mappings into the cost-model repo; @samir add burst_uplift param and spot preemption CSV ingest; @olivia collect API endpoint examples from each partner by EOD Fri.

olivia: got it — i'll ping partners and collate. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
